story_type: crewed spacecraft power system trouble right after launch, mission continued day by day
hook: Their power started failing, with eight days still to go.
narration: Right after launch, their new power system started failing. They were supposed to stay up for eight days.
This was Gemini 5 in August 1965, the first real endurance test, with Gordon Cooper and Pete Conrad aboard.
The new system was fuel cells, which make electricity by combining hydrogen and oxygen.
Back home, the headlines read Ailing Gemini 5, and Fuel Troubles Cripple Gemini.
Flight director Chris Kraft decided to keep going, one day at a time.
[short pause] Recovery ships stood by around the world, in case it came down early.
outcome: Gemini 5 flew its full eight days and splashed down. Mission complete.
title: Gemini 5 power failing, 8 days to go
description:
Gemini 5 launched in August 1965 on the first eight-day endurance flight with Gordon Cooper and Pete Conrad. Problems in its new power supply put the mission in doubt, and flight director Chris Kraft kept it going day by day.
